I am an old woman, I never went to school, and this small maize plot near my house is what feeds us. Last year I got the coupon from the government and I bought one bag of 23-21-0 and one bag of urea — I hope this year the coupon comes again, because without it I cannot buy fertilizer from the shop. I always put the manure from my goats and the ash from the kitchen on this plot before the rains, because my mother did the same. I buy the hybrid maize seed, the one my neighbor Mayi Banda grows, because it gives more cobs — but only a small packet, enough for this plot, and I keep some local seed for the other garden.

I do not buy medicine for the maize, I just pull the weeds with my hoe, me and my daughter. The plot is right behind my house, there is no river close, so I only wait for the rain. When the fall armyworm comes I pick them by hand in the morning, that is what the women here do. I do not hire people for such a small piece of land — my daughter and my grandchildren help me, and sometimes I help my sister and she helps me back.
